statement_record.book: For any small category C the functor category Set^C is cartesian closed: G^F(c) := Nat(C(c,-) x F, G), functorial in c by precomposition with f^*, and by Yoneda one gets the bijection {H x F => G} = {H => G^F} natural in H, with evaluation ev : G^F x F => G as the counit and explicit mutually inverse transposition formulas.
statement_record.intree: @Cartesian (@Fun C D) whenever D is cartesian (Instance/Fun/Cartesian.v:111) — products only; and @Closed Sets (Instance/Sets/Cartesian/Closed.v:38) — the exponential in Sets alone.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the library proves only the CARTESIAN half of 'cartesian closed' for a functor category, and the CLOSED half only for the base Sets (i.e. Riehl's lemma at C = 1). The exponential functor G^F on [C, Sets], the Yoneda-based formula, the natural bijection (4.4.12)/(4.4.13), and the ev/transposition formulas are all missing.

evidence.intree_statement: Class SymMonClosed := { smc_is_symmetric : @SymmetricMonoidal C; exponent_obj : obj -> obj -> obj where "x => y" := (exponent_obj x y); exp_iso {x y z} : x (x) y ~> z ≊ x ~> y => z; curry' {x y z} := to exp_iso; uncurry' {x y z} := from exp_iso; eval' {x y} : (x => y) (x) x ~> y := uncurry' id; ump_exponents' {x y z} (f : x (x) y ~> z) : ∃! h : x ~> y => z, f ≈ eval' ∘ (h (x) id) }

Class ClosedMonoidal := { closed_is_cartesian : @CartesianMonoidal C; exponent_obj : obj -> obj -> obj; exp_iso {x y z} : x (x) y ~> z ≊ x ~> y => z; ...; ump_exponents' {x y z} (f : x (x) y ~> z) : ∃! h : x ~> y => z, f ≈ eval' ∘ (h (x) id) }  (* the mainline class: its tensor IS the cartesian product *)

statement_record.book: A closed monoidal category generalizes a cartesian closed category to the case where the left adjoint bifunctor of a two-variable adjunction need not be the categorical product: 'closed' names the existence of left and right closures for the tensor, 'monoidal' the tensor together with coherent natural isomorphisms (full definition deferred to section E.2).
statement_record.intree: SymMonClosed = SymmetricMonoidal base + internal hom `exponent_obj` + the tensor-hom hom-set iso `exp_iso {x y z} : x (x) y ~> z ≊ x ~> y => z` + `ump_exponents'` in ∃!-form. ClosedMonoidal is the same record but with `closed_is_cartesian : @CartesianMonoidal C`.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker on both available classes. (a) `ClosedMonoidal`, the library's headline 'closed monoidal category', hard-requires the tensor to be the CARTESIAN monoidal structure — it is precisely the special case Riehl's gloss is generalizing away from, and Construction/Funny/Closed.v:30-34 records this as a structural no-go for non-cartesian tensors. (b) `SymMonClosed` is the genuine general class but bundles SYMMETRIC monoidal, an extra hypothesis Riehl does not impose; under symmetry the two closures coincide, so the left/right-closure distinction of the book's gloss cannot even be stated.

gap: There is no closed-monoidal class over a bare `Monoidal`: `grep -rn --include='*.v' "Class .*Closed"` yields ClosedMonoidal (cartesian-bundled), SymMonClosed (symmetry-bundled), Structure/Cartesian/Closed.v's `Closed` (cartesian), CompactClosed, and Structure/Closed.v:166's Eilenberg-Kelly `Class Closed`, which is COMMENTED OUT and does not typecheck (its own header: 'the class does not yet typecheck ... the whole block is left commented out'). Consequently: no `biclosed` predicate (`grep -i biclosed` = 12 hits, all prose), no separate left- and right-closure operations, and no proof that they agree under symmetry. Additionally SymMonClosed has NO in-tree instance (its header's SCOPE paragraph, Structure/Monoidal/StarAutonomous.v:67, states 'No concrete instance is constructed here.'; `rg 'SymMonClosed'` returns only the class declaration and header prose), so nothing witnesses a non-cartesian closed monoidal category through the class interface. A genuine non-cartesian monoidal closed structure IS developed in-tree, but deliberately outside every class: Construction/Funny/Closed.v proves the beta/eta laws and uniqueness for the funny-tensor internal hom (`funny_curry_beta` :210, `funny_curry_unique` :222) while its header explains why neither ClosedMonoidal nor Theory/Adjunction.v can express it.

statement_record.book: For a bifunctor F : A x B -> C: (i) if each F(a,-) has a right adjoint G_a then there is a UNIQUE bifunctor G : A^op x C -> B with G(a,-) = G_a making C(F(a,b),c) ≅ B(b,G(a,c)) natural in all three variables; (ii) dually for F(-,b) and H : B^op x C -> A; (iii) when both hold, G(-,c) and H(-,c) are MUTUAL RIGHT ADJOINTS for each c.
statement_record.intree: InternalHomFunctor : C^op ∏ C ⟶ C, the assembled right-adjoint bifunctor for the single bifunctor F = (- × -) over a cartesian closed C, built by hand from `curry`/`eval` rather than derived from an assembly theorem; plus curry_comp_l / curry_comp, which are naturality of the transpose in the source and target variables.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: special case only (F is the product bifunctor of a `Closed` category, whose exp_iso is already a class FIELD indexed by all three variables, so nothing is assembled from pointwise data), no uniqueness clause, no statement of three-variable naturality as such, and clause (iii) has no counterpart at all.

gap: Nothing in the tree quantifies over an arbitrary bifunctor F : A ∏ B ⟶ C with pointwise right adjoints. The one-variable analogue Theory/Universal/Arrow.v:214 `AdjunctionFromUniversalArrows` is Proposition 4.4.4, a different item.
